records.source: SpaceX Flight 15 return plan as reported by Autonocion and Tesla Oracle (Nov 2026): two catch fittings directly under the forward flaps, each protruding about one foot (Eric Berger, Ars Technica)
records.conditions: Pin centre 0.4 m below the lower end of the modelled forward-flap hinge line (hinge_y_m −6.25, length 5.7 m), on the same ±Z sides as the flaps. With a 4.4 m lateral offset and 0.4 m radius the pin stands 0.3 m proud of the 4.5 m hull. The former +5.0 m station sat in the ogive, where the hull radius is below the pin offset.
records.uncertainty: Station along the axis is inferred from the description; SpaceX published no dimensions.

records.source: Same Flight 15 fitting description, applied to the earlier ship nose
records.conditions: Pin centre just below the lower end of the modelled forward-flap hinge line (hinge_y_m −6.0, length 5.7 m).
records.uncertainty: Inferred station; SpaceX published no dimensions.

records.source: Exosphere two-pin static load budget for the Flight 15 entry chapter
records.conditions: At 225 t and 9.81 m/s², two matched supports deflect about 0.44 m each. The existing 0.60 m travel, 3 MN load and 5 m cradle radius limits apply. Guidance cuts the engines only when the predicted first compression peak stays within 90 % of the travel and load limits.
records.uncertainty: Effective compliance chosen for the simulated mass envelope. Actual pin, arm and vehicle stiffness and loads are unpublished in the mission material.

records.source: Exosphere two-pin static load budget for a Super Heavy catch
records.conditions: Sized for a 300 t catch envelope (214 t dry part plus landing reserve): two matched supports deflect 0.35 m each under 9.81 m/s². The former 1.2 MN/m default deflected 0.87 m at the 214 t dry mass, beyond the 0.60 m travel, so a settle that rejects over-travel could never accept a booster.
records.uncertainty: Effective compliance chosen for the simulated mass envelope. Actual pin, arm and vehicle stiffness and loads are unpublished.

records.source: Exosphere two-pin static load budget for a Super Heavy catch
records.conditions: Same 300 t catch envelope and 0.35 m static deflection as the V3 booster.
records.uncertainty: Effective compliance chosen for the simulated mass envelope. Actual pin, arm and vehicle stiffness and loads are unpublished.

records.source: Flight 5 booster and Flight 15 ship catch coverage: the caught vehicle hangs above Orbital Launch Pad 2's mount
records.conditions: The carriage rides to the vehicle's pin height plus this clearance above the 19.8 m mount top. The Flight 15 ship then catches at about 62 m, the Super Heavy near 90 m, instead of the former fixed 55 m that left the ship's tail 3 m above grade.
records.uncertainty: No published catch height or clearance; reports only state that the ship hung above the mount.

records.source: Flight 15 coverage: the ship descended between open arms that then closed onto its two fittings
records.conditions: Half the open gap from the cradle centreline. With a 4.5 m hull the axis may be up to 5.5 m to either side and the closing arms still stop against the hull under the fittings. Replaces the 5 m capture disc, which accepted only ±0.6 m along the pin axis.
records.uncertainty: Pad 2 arm opening is unpublished; SpaceX states only that the arms were shortened and made faster.

records.source: Image-derived arm proportions; catch fittings protrude about one foot (Eric Berger, Ars Technica, via Autonocion)
records.conditions: Rail on top of each arm from the hull outward. A fitting rests on it while it stands proud of the hull over the rail, which bounds roll about the axis to roughly ±20°.
